#compdef hlp

# zsh completion for hlp, generated by `hlp completion zsh`.
# Use it with: hlp completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_hlp"  (then restart the shell)
_hlp() {
    local curcontext="$curcontext" state state_descr line ret=1
    typeset -A opt_args
    _arguments -C \
        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[show this help message and exit]' \
        '--version[show program'\''s version number and exit]' \
        '(--verbose --debug)'{--verbose,--debug}'[Log each request to stderr (method, path, status, milliseconds, retries) and what was read, never the API key (before the command)]' \
        '--demo[Run the command on synthetic data\: no .env or implicit settings file is read and no controller is contacted (before the command; not with doctor, snapshot, diff or --notify)]' \
        '--timeout[Seconds to wait for each request to the controller (before the command; default\: UNIFI_TIMEOUT from .env, else 15)]:SECONDS: ' \
        '--parallel[How many requests to make at once (before the command; 1 means one by one; default\: UNIFI_PARALLEL_REQUESTS from .env, else 6)]:N: ' \
        '--site[Which site to read\: its name, internal reference (such as default) or UUID (before the command; default\: UNIFI_SITE_ID from .env, else default)]:NAME|REF|UUID: ' \
        '--env-file[Read settings from this .env file (before the command). Default\: $HLP_ENV, else ./.env in the current directory]:FILE:_files' \
        '--color[Terminal colors\: auto (a terminal that supports them, unless NO_COLOR is set), always (also when piped, but never in --json/--csv/export/completion output) or never (before the command; needs the pretty extra; default\: auto)]:WHEN:(auto always never)' \
        '--no-progress[Never show transient progress on stderr (before the command; progress is also off when stderr is not a terminal, with --plain, --verbose or machine-readable output)]' \
        '--plain[Plain text only\: no color, animation, decorative headings or symbols, whatever --color says (before the command)]' \
        '1: :->command' \
        '*:: :->args' && ret=0

    case $state in
        command)
            local -a commands
            commands=(
                'audit:Configuration audit\: settings that are probably not what you want'
                'client:Troubleshoot one client\: where it attaches, link quality and related findings'
                'completion:Print a shell completion script (bash, zsh or fish)'
                'diagnose:Run read-only health checks (offline devices, port errors, ...)'
                'diff:What changed\: compare saved snapshots, or a snapshot against the live network'
                'doctor:Check the installation and the settings, and that the controller answers'
                'events:Event history from the controller log\: disconnects, roams, IP conflicts...'
                'export:Export clients, devices and switch ports to CSV'
                'firewall:Firewall policies, port forwards and the zone matrix, with what looks wrong'
                'info:Show controller version and available sites'
                'init:Guided first-time setup\: write .env, hlp.toml and snapshots/ for you'
                'new-clients:List clients that are in no client group (all known clients)'
                'query:List and filter devices, clients, reservations, switch ports, networks and Wi-Fi networks'
                'serve:Serve the read-only web API on this machine (needs the web extra)'
                'snapshot:Save the current inventory to a local JSON file, for `diff` later'
                'topology:Draw the uplink tree\: gateway, switches and APs with ports, speeds and problems'
                'wan:Internet health\: current state, 24-hour monitoring and speedtest history'
                'web-user:Manage the accounts of the web interface\: users, roles and passwords'
                'wifi:Wireless report\: each AP'\''s radios and a channel plan from the neighboring networks'
            )
            _describe -t commands 'hlp command' commands && ret=0
            ;;
        args)
            case $line[1] in
                audit)
                    _arguments \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[show this help message and exit]' \
                        '--fail-on[Lowest severity that gives a non-zero exit code (default\: warning)]:fail-on:(info warning)' \
                        '--config[TOML file with an ignore list (default\: ./hlp.toml if present)]:FILE:_files' \
                        '--show-ignored[Also list the findings suppressed by the ignore list]' \
                        '--no-emoji[Use text severity labels (automatic when output is not a UTF-8 terminal)]' \
                        '--json[Print the findings as JSON (with a stable code each)]' && ret=0
                    ;;
                client)
                    _arguments \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[show this help message and exit]' \
                        '--json[Output JSON instead of text]' \
                        '--config[TOML file with diagnose thresholds and ignore list (default\: ./hlp.toml if present)]:FILE:_files' \
                        '--no-events[Skip the recent-events section, which otherwise sends the one approved read-only event-log query]' \
                        '--since[How far back the recent events reach, e.g. 12h, 7d (default\: 24h)]:DURATION: ' \
                        '--no-emoji[Use text severity labels (automatic when output is not a UTF-8 terminal)]' && ret=0
                    ;;
                completion)
                    _arguments \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[show this help message and exit]' \
                        '1:completion:(bash zsh fish)' && ret=0
                    ;;
                diagnose)
                    _arguments \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[show this help message and exit]' \
                        '--fail-on[Lowest severity that gives a non-zero exit code (default\: warning); critical always exits 2]:fail-on:(info warning critical)' \
                        '--config[TOML file with thresholds and an ignore list (default\: ./hlp.toml if present)]:FILE:_files' \
                        '--only[Run only the checks of these areas (devices, health, wan, clients, reservations, ports, wifi, events); repeatable. Only the data they need is read]:AREA\[,AREA...\]:_values -s , AREA\[,AREA...\] devices health wan clients reservations ports wifi events' \
                        '--skip[Run every check except those of these areas (same names); repeatable. Skipping events sends no event-log request]:AREA\[,AREA...\]:_values -s , AREA\[,AREA...\] devices health wan clients reservations ports wifi events' \
                        '--no-events[Skip the event-log checks (repeated disconnects, IP conflicts, ...), which otherwise send the one approved read-only POST; same as --skip events]' \
                        '--since[How far back the event checks look, e.g. 12h, 7d (default\: 24h)]:DURATION: ' \
                        '--show-ignored[Also list the findings suppressed by the ignore list]' \
                        '--no-emoji[Use text severity labels (automatic when output is not a UTF-8 terminal)]' \
                        '--json[Print the findings as JSON (with a stable code per check); exit codes are unchanged]' \
                        '--watch[Run the checks again every SECONDS (10 to 86400) and print only what changed (new, worse, fixed) until Ctrl-C; not with --json or --notify]:SECONDS: ' \
                        '--notify[Send a notification (ntfy, a webhook and/or email, set in .env) when findings are new, worse or fixed since the last notified run; this is the only thing that sends data off this machine]' \
                        '--notify-min[with --notify\: lowest severity to notify about (default\: warning)]:SEVERITY:(info warning critical)' \
                        '--notify-redact[with --notify\: send only the generic description of each check, no names, addresses or MACs]' \
                        '--notify-dry-run[with --notify\: print what would be sent to stderr, send nothing, keep the state]' \
                        '--notify-baseline[with --notify\: record the current findings as already reported and send nothing (avoids a first message about everything)]' \
                        '--notify-state[with --notify\: where reported findings are remembered (default\: snapshots/<site id>/notify-state.json, one file per site)]:FILE:_files' && ret=0
                    ;;
                diff)
                    _arguments \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[show this help message and exit]' \
                        '--dir[Snapshot directory (default\: this site'\''s directory in ./snapshots/; finding it asks the controller which site is meant, so give --dir to work offline)]:DIR:_files' \
                        '--last-two[Compare the two newest saved snapshots (no controller needed)]' \
                        '--all[List every client connect/disconnect and IP change instead of the first few]' \
                        '--json[Output JSON instead of text]' \
                        '*:snapshot:_files' && ret=0
                    ;;
                doctor)
                    _arguments \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[show this help message and exit]' \
                        '--offline[Only check the installation and the settings files; do not contact the controller]' \
                        '--no-events[Skip the event-log check (the one read-only POST)]' \
                        '--config[TOML settings file to check (default\: ./hlp.toml if present)]:FILE:_files' \
                        '--json[Print the checks as JSON]' && ret=0
                    ;;
                events)
                    _arguments \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[show this help message and exit]' \
                        '--since[How far back to look, e.g. 90m, 24h, 7d, 2w (default\: 24h)]:DURATION: ' \
                        '--category[Only this category, e.g. CLIENT_DEVICES, UNIFI_DEVICES, INTERNET_AND_WAN, AUDIT (repeatable)]:NAME: ' \
                        '--severity[Only this severity (repeatable)]:severity:(low medium high)' \
                        '--event[Only event types containing TEXT, e.g. roam, disconnected, ip_conflict]:TEXT: ' \
                        '--client[Only events about this client (name, hostname, IP or part of a MAC)]:NAME|MAC|IP: ' \
                        '--device[Only events about this UniFi device (e.g. an AP or switch)]:NAME|IP: ' \
                        '(-s --search)'{-s,--search}'[Text search done by the controller]:search: ' \
                        '--limit[Most events to show, newest first (default 100; 0 for all)]:limit: ' \
                        '--summary[Counts by type and the noisiest clients/devices over the whole window (ignores --limit) instead of a list]' \
                        '--json[Output JSON instead of a table]' && ret=0
                    ;;
                export)
                    _arguments \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[show this help message and exit]' \
                        '(-o --output-dir)'{-o,--output-dir}'[Directory for the files (default\: current directory)]:file:_files' \
                        '--format[csv\: unifi_clients.csv and one CSV per switch (default); json\: one file, unifi_inventory.json, with the same data]:format:(csv json)' \
                        '--include-offline[Also list previously seen clients that are not connected]' && ret=0
                    ;;
                firewall)
                    _arguments \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[show this help message and exit]' \
                        '--all[Also list the built-in policies (by default only the ones you defined)]' \
                        '--zones[Also show each zone'\''s networks and the zone matrix]' \
                        '--search[Only policies and port forwards with this text in any column]:TEXT: ' \
                        '--no-emoji[Use text severity labels (automatic when output is not a UTF-8 terminal)]' \
                        '--json[Output JSON instead of text]' && ret=0
                    ;;
                info)
                    _arguments \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[show this help message and exit]' && ret=0
                    ;;
                init)
                    _arguments \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[show this help message and exit]' \
                        '--dir[Where to write .env, hlp.toml and snapshots/ (default\: the current directory)]:DIR:_files' \
                        '--url[The controller'\''s address, such as https\://192.168.1.1]:URL: ' \
                        '--site[The site to use (default\: default)]:NAME: ' \
                        '--verify[Check the controller'\''s certificate (true, the default), do not (false), or against this CA file]:true|false|FILE: ' \
                        '--api-key-stdin[Read the API key from one line of standard input and ask nothing else (needs --url); a key is never an argument]' \
                        '--no-input[Ask nothing\: use only the options and what the existing .env holds]' \
                        '--force[Do not ask before replacing the settings in an existing .env]' \
                        '--check[Afterwards read the controller once to check the address, the key and the site]' && ret=0
                    ;;
                new-clients)
                    _arguments \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[show this help message and exit]' \
                        '(-s --search)'{-s,--search}'[Case-insensitive substring match on any field]:search: ' \
                        '--json[Output JSON instead of a table]' && ret=0
                    ;;
                query)
                    _arguments \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[show this help message and exit]' \
                        '(-s --search)'{-s,--search}'[Case-insensitive substring match on any field]:search: ' \
                        '--include-offline[Also list previously seen clients that are not connected]' \
                        '--json[Output JSON instead of a table]' \
                        '--csv[Output CSV instead of a table (the columns of --json; text that a spreadsheet would run as a formula gets a leading '\'')]' \
                        '--switch[ports only\: switch name (case-insensitive substring)]:switch: ' \
                        '--down[ports only\: only ports that are down]' \
                        '--errors[ports only\: only ports with rx/tx errors]' \
                        '--network[clients only\: connected clients on a network (name, case-insensitive substring)]:NAME: ' \
                        '--ssid[clients only\: connected clients on a Wi-Fi network (SSID, case-insensitive substring)]:NAME: ' \
                        '--ap[clients only\: connected clients on an access point (name, case-insensitive substring)]:NAME: ' \
                        '--offline[reservations only\: only clients offline long enough for `diagnose` to report them (reserved_offline_warn_days), or never seen]' \
                        '--config[reservations --offline only\: TOML file with the threshold (default\: ./hlp.toml if present)]:FILE:_files' \
                        '1:query:(all devices clients reservations ports networks wlans)' && ret=0
                    ;;
                serve)
                    _arguments \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[show this help message and exit]' \
                        '--host[The address to listen on (default 127.0.0.1, this machine only). Another address makes the server reachable from the network\: logins then need TLS in front (see --forwarded-allow-ips)]:ADDRESS: ' \
                        '--allowed-host[A name the server is reached by, such as hlp.lan or 192.168.1.5 (repeatable). A request with another Host header is refused. Required with --host 0.0.0.0 or \:\:; wildcards are not accepted]:NAME: ' \
                        '--forwarded-allow-ips[Believe X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto from these reverse proxies (addresses or networks, comma-separated); by default from none. * and 0.0.0.0/0 are not accepted]:IPS: ' \
                        '--allow-public-controller[Let the guided setup (a server with no settings) connect to a controller on a public address; by default it only connects to addresses on your own network]' \
                        '--read-only[Write no file on this machine\: the settings editor and the setup'\''s files answer 403 (logging in and the audit log still work)]' \
                        '--scheduler[Run diagnose (and notify) and take snapshots on a timer inside the server (SCHEDULER_DIAGNOSE_MINUTES, SCHEDULER_SNAPSHOT_HOURS, SCHEDULER_SNAPSHOT_KEEP); it writes files, so not with --read-only]' \
                        '--port[The port to listen on (default 8787)]:PORT: ' \
                        '--data-dir[Where the server keeps its own files (default\: the current directory)]:DIR:_files' \
                        '--config[TOML file with diagnose thresholds and ignore list (default\: ./hlp.toml if present)]:FILE:_files' && ret=0
                    ;;
                snapshot)
                    _arguments \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[show this help message and exit]' \
                        '(-o --output)'{-o,--output}'[Write to this file instead of a timestamped one in --dir]:FILE:_files' \
                        '--dir[Directory for timestamped snapshots (default\: ./snapshots/<site id>/, one directory per site)]:DIR:_files' \
                        '--keep[Afterwards delete the oldest snapshots in --dir (of this site, by default), keeping the newest N]:N: ' \
                        '--force[Allow -o to replace an existing file]' && ret=0
                    ;;
                topology)
                    _arguments \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[show this help message and exit]' \
                        '--clients[Also list the wired clients under each device]' \
                        '--format[text\: the tree (default); mermaid\: a Mermaid flowchart; dot\: a Graphviz digraph. The graph formats cannot be combined with --json]:format:(text mermaid dot)' \
                        '--json[Output nested JSON instead of a tree]' \
                        '--config[TOML file with diagnose thresholds and ignore list (default\: ./hlp.toml if present)]:FILE:_files' \
                        '--no-emoji[Use ASCII drawing and text severity labels (automatic when output is not a UTF-8 terminal); no effect on the graph formats]' && ret=0
                    ;;
                wan)
                    _arguments \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[show this help message and exit]' \
                        '--days[How many days of speedtests to summarize (default\: 30)]:N: ' \
                        '--json[Output JSON instead of text]' \
                        '--config[TOML file with the thresholds (default\: ./hlp.toml if present)]:FILE:_files' && ret=0
                    ;;
                web-user)
                    _arguments \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[show this help message and exit]' \
                        '--role[add\: the role of the new user (default viewer); set-role\: the new role]:role:(viewer admin)' \
                        '--password-stdin[add and reset-password\: read the password from one line of standard input instead of asking for it (a password is never an argument)]' \
                        '--data-dir[Where users.json and audit.log are kept (default\: the current directory)]:DIR:_files' \
                        '1:web-user:(add list set-role disable enable delete reset-password)' && ret=0
                    ;;
                wifi)
                    _arguments \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[show this help message and exit]' \
                        '--band[Only this band]:2.4|5|6:(2.4 5 6)' \
                        '--ap[Only this AP (name or part of it), and only neighbors it hears]:NAME: ' \
                        '--min-signal[Neighbors weaker than this are counted but not named or compared (default -80)]:DBM: ' \
                        '--all[Name every strong neighbor on a channel, not just the first few]' \
                        '--json[Output JSON instead of text]' && ret=0
                    ;;
            esac
            ;;
    esac
    return ret
}

if [ "$funcstack[1]" = "_hlp" ]; then
    _hlp "$@"
else
    compdef _hlp hlp
fi
